transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, I guess the main thing is during these long sales strategy meetings at work, I keep getting up even though I know I’m supposed to stay seated. Like, I’ll tell myself I’m just refilling my water or going to stand by the printer for a second, but it’s really more that I can’t seem to just sit there the whole time.  

And I know everyone probably gets bored in those meetings — I mean, some of them go on forever, and half the time we’re talking about projections that change the next week anyway — but it’s started to feel noticeable, like I’m the one popping up more than I should.
When you feel the urge to get up in those meetings, is it mainly because you feel anxious or keyed up?

I don’t think it’s mostly anxiety, exactly. It’s more like… I just can’t stay in the chair through the whole long meeting. Like I’ll make an excuse to refill my water, or I’ll end up pacing near the printer for a minute, even though I know I’m supposed to just sit there.

I mean, sometimes the meetings are stressful because sales numbers are sales numbers, and everyone has opinions, but the getting up feels more like this pull to move than me panicking or anything.
When you were a child, were you also the kind of person who had trouble staying seated when you were expected to?

I’m not totally sure about when I was a kid, honestly. I’d have to think about that or maybe ask my parents, because what’s really standing out to me now is the work thing — these long sales strategy meetings where I know I’m supposed to stay seated, and I still keep finding reasons to get up, like refilling my water or wandering over by the printer.

I mean, those meetings are kind of their own special kind of torture, but still… it feels like I’m up more than I should be.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or euphoric for several days in a row?

Um… unusually energized or euphoric for several days? I don’t know. I mean, I have good days, like if I close a decent account at work I’ll be kind of excited and talk everyone’s ear off, but that’s more just being relieved because sales can be such a roller coaster.

I’m not sure I’ve noticed anything that I’d call euphoric for days in a row, though. What do you mean by “unusually” exactly?
Have you ever gone for several days needing much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

I don’t think so… not in that way. I mean, I definitely have nights where I stay up too late, like scrolling or thinking about work stuff, and then the next day I’m running on coffee and kind of pretending I’m fine. But needing less sleep and still feeling great for several days? I’m not sure I’ve had that.

My sleep can get weird when work is busy, especially if I’m trying to prep for a pitch or I’m worried about a client, but I usually feel it the next day. I’m not, like, magically full of energy.
Do you spend a lot of your day worrying about many different things?

I’m not sure I’d say “many different things” all day. I mean, I worry about work, definitely — like clients and numbers and whether I forgot to follow up with someone — but that kind of feels baked into sales, you know?

Then again, sometimes I’ll be thinking about one thing and suddenly I’m thinking about my car needing an oil change or whether I replied to a text from my sister, but I don’t know if that’s worry exactly or just my brain hopping around. Sorry, I’m probably not answering that cleanly. Could you say what you mean by “a lot of the day”?
Do you often find that once you start worrying, it’s hard to stop or control the worry?

I guess… sometimes? Like if I realize I forgot to email someone back, I’ll keep circling back to it in my head, and then I’ll open my inbox and somehow end up looking at three other things, which doesn’t really help.

But I don’t know if I’d say I can’t control the worry exactly. It’s more like my attention gets stuck on something for a bit and then jumps somewhere else. I’m not sure if that counts as worry being hard to stop.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because your attention drifts?

Yeah, that happens. I’ll get, like, most of the way through something — a proposal, or updating the CRM after a client call — and then somehow I don’t do the last little piece.

Like I’ll have the final version basically ready, and then I mean to send it, but I get pulled into something else or notice another email, and later I’m like, wait, did I actually send that? Or I’ll talk to someone and plan the follow-up, but then I don’t log it. It’s annoying because it’s not like I didn’t care or didn’t know what to do — it’s usually just the last step that slips.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying seated at school?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I remember it starting way before high school. In elementary school my teachers would write things like I was bright, but I rushed through work or talked out of turn.

And I remember my desk being just… stuffed with half-finished papers and old homework sheets. Homework was a whole thing too — I’d do it and then forget to turn it in, or lose it in my backpack. Well, I guess that’s still the same theme. So yes, before 12, definitely some of that was there.
